BURSEVI:v5p172/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172/r1.claim: They separated from their people in belief and resolved to separate physically by fleeing for their religion.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r1.anchor: الاعتزال بالفارسية (جداشدن) أي : فارقتموهم في الاعتقاد وأردتم الاعتزال الجسماني

BURSEVI:v5p172/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p172/r2.claim: After Decianus challenged them and gave them respite, Yamlīkhā, their leader, spoke to them on the road as they fled.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (قبل أزين كذشت كه دقيانوس بعد از معارضه ايشان مهلت داد

BURSEVI:v5p172/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172/r3.claim: The clause about what they worship may be a relative or a verbal noun; the exception is connected if they were polytheists like Meccans, but disconnected if they worshipped only idols.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r3.anchor: عطف على الضمير المنصوب وما مصدرية أو موصولة أي : إذا اعتزلتموهم ومعبوديهم

BURSEVI:v5p172/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r4.speaker: الفراء
BURSEVI:v5p172/r4.claim: He treats take refuge in the cave as the answer to إذ, like saying: when you do something, then do this.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r4.anchor: قال الفراء هو جواب إذ كما تقول إذ فعلت فافعل كذا

BURSEVI:v5p172/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172/r5.claim: The cave command may indicate the unstated answer: inward separation from the people entails bodily withdrawal, or those wishing to leave should take refuge there.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r5.anchor: وقيل هو دليل على جوابه أي : إذ اعتزلتموهم اعتزالا اعتقاديا فاعتزلوهم اعتزالا جسمانيا

BURSEVI:v5p172/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172/r6.claim: Ideological separation entails bodily withdrawal; Rasteghfanī consequently ruled out marriage between Sunnis and Muʿtazilites.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الاعتزال الاعتقادي يوجب الاعتزال الجسماني

BURSEVI:v5p172/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r7.speaker: رستغفني
BURSEVI:v5p172/r7.claim: Asked about marriage between Sunnis and Muʿtazilites, he ruled it impermissible.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r7.anchor: سئل الرستغفني عن المناكحة بين أهل السنة وبين أهل الاعتزال فقال : لا يجوز

BURSEVI:v5p172/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172/r8.claim: God expands His favor in both worlds and makes their flight for religion easy and beneficial; their certainty and trust explain their confidence.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r8.anchor: يبسط لكم ويوسع عليكم {ربكم} مالك أمركم

BURSEVI:v5p172/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p172/r9.claim: A hadith instructs people to call on God while certain of receiving an answer.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ادعوا الله وأنتم موقنون بالإجابة"

BURSEVI:v5p172/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172/r10.claim: The verse inwardly describes a sincere seeker leaving bad companions, worshipping God alone, turning from everything else, and relying on God as he flees to Him.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r10.anchor: إشارة إلى أن التائب الصادق والطالب المحق من اعتزل عن قومه وترك أهل صحبته

BURSEVI:v5p172/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172/r11.speaker: الحجندي
BURSEVI:v5p172/r11.claim: His verse teaches that union is attained only by severance, beginning with cutting oneself off from everything else.
BURSEVI:v5p172/r11.anchor: قال الحجندي : وصل ميسر نشود جز بقطع قطع نخست از همه ببريدنست

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r1.claim: The continuation of the quoted verse praises retreat as a pleasant state for someone who inhabits the corner of seclusion.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r1.anchor: خوش وقت آنكه معتكف كنج عزلتست

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r2.claim: The seeker should cling to a perfected guide who trains him, increases his guidance, and strengthens his heart through spiritual care.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r2.anchor: متمسكا بذيل إرادة شيخ كامل مكمل واصل موصل ليربيه ويزيد في هدايته

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r3.claim: A Mathnawī couplet warns that walking without a guide breeds self-conceit, error, and humiliation, and urges following the shaykh to receive his aid.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r3.anchor: كره شيرى ون روى ره بى دليل خويش بيني در ضلالي وذليل

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r4.claim: The Cave youths were unusually drawn by God and raised without an intermediary; this is rare, while the normal way is guidance through prophets and then learned scholars and shaykhs.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r4.anchor: ولكنهم كانوا مجذوبين من الله مربوبين بربهم وذلك من النوادر ولا حكم للنادر

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said that God educated him and made his education excellent, illustrating direct divine instruction.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r5.anchor: وإليه يشير قوله عليه السلام : "إن الله أدبني فأحسن تأديبي"

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r6.claim: Taking refuge in the cave inwardly means retreating into solitude and holding to guides who lead along the Sufi path.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r6.anchor: ففي قوله : {فأووا إلى الكهف} إشارة إلى الالتجاء بالخلوة والتمسك بالمشايخ المسلكين

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r7.claim: Special mercy means God's personal favor, drawing seekers into His attributes so they acquire their qualities; general mercy is shared by believers and unbelievers, jinn, humans, and animals.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r7.anchor: أي : ينشر لكم طريق الوصول والوصال كما في "التأويلات النجمية"

BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r8.claim: The prepared benefit is an opened path to arrival and union with God.
BURSEVI:v5p172#2/r8.anchor: أي : ينشر لكم طريق الوصول والوصال كما في "التأويلات النجمية"

QASHANI:18:16/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:16/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:16/r1.claim: Separation means disengaging from selves and faculties; retreat to the body permits disciplined use of bodily tools for knowledge and action, with voluntary death from lower impulses.
QASHANI:18:16/r1.anchor: إلى البدن لاستعمال الآلات البدنية في الاستكمال بالعلوم والأعمال

QASHANI:18:16/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:16/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:16/r2.claim: God's mercy gives true life through knowledge, while its utility is delight in witnessing and perfection; a cited verse describes one formerly dead who receives light.
QASHANI:18:16/r2.anchor: ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته } حياة حقيقية بالعلم والمعرفة

QASHANI:18:16/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:16/r3.speaker: عليه السلام
QASHANI:18:16/r3.claim: A saying about Abū Bakr calls him a dead man walking on earth, meaning dead to himself and walking through God.
QASHANI:18:16/r3.anchor: من أراد أن ينظر ميتا يمشي على وجه الأرض فلينظر أبا بكر

QASHANI:18:16/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:16/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:16/r4.claim: Alternatively, leaving the community's idols and desires means retreating into bodily caves, limiting excess and practicing discipline; God gives celestial aid and a useful path through which others may be guided.
QASHANI:18:16/r4.anchor: اعتزلتم قومكم ومعبوداتهم غير الله من مطالبهم المختلفة

QASHANI:18:16/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:16/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:16/r5.claim: The cave refuge hints at the Mahdi entering a cave before emergence and Jesus's descent; latent mercy unfolds through bodily attachment and its preparations for perfection.
QASHANI:18:16/r5.anchor: يفهم من دخول المهدي في الغار إذ أخرج ونزل عيسى

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r1.claim: They read مرفق with kasra on mīm and fatḥa on fāʾ; al-Kisai also transmits the opposite vowel pattern through Abu Bakr from Asim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: مرفقا بكسر الميم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r2.claim: They read مرفق with fatḥa on mīm and kasra on fāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر: (مرفقا) بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda says مرفق can mean something used for comfort or support; in the arm it names the elbow.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r3.anchor: أبو عبيدة: المرفق: ما ارتفقت به، وبعضهم يقول

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r4.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats both vowel patterns as lexical variants: مرفق can name an aid or be a noun like المسجد, without a difference in meaning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p130/r4.anchor: مرفقا ومرفقا: لغتان لا فرق بينهما أيضا، هما اسمان

QIRAAT-ER:18:16:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:16:19#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:16:19#1/r1.claim: Replacing hamza with yāʾ softens the glottal stop, with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:18:16:19#1/r1.anchor: Hamza replaced by yāʾ — softening of glottal stop; no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:18:16:23#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:16:23#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:16:23#1/r1.claim: Marfiq may mean the elbow or a useful thing, shifting from an instrumental to a locative or nominal pattern.
QIRAAT-ER:18:16:23#1/r1.anchor: Alternate canonical vocalization: marfiq (mafʿil pattern) = the elbow specifically, or a useful thing

QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r4.claim: Detachment from everything besides God brings union with God; those who left idolatry were sheltered by divine care.
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r4.anchor: العزلة عن غير الله توجب الوصلة بالله

QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r5.claim: One who relinquishes self-directed plans, returns sincerely to God, and relies on no peer is sheltered, relieved of burdens, and given a place in divine favor.
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r5.anchor: ويقال من تبرأ من اختياره في احتياله ، وصدق رجوعه إلى الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r1.claim: The youths address one another; withdrawing from their people means both leaving their homeland and rejecting their beliefs, a bodily and inward separation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r1.anchor: والاعتزال يشمل مفارقة أوطان قومهم ومعتقداتهم فهو اعتزال جسماني وقلبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r2.claim: ما is coordinated with the object of اعتزلتموهم; the exception is connected if their people worshipped God along with idols.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r2.anchor: وما معطوف على المفعول في اعتزلتموهم أي واعتزلتم معبودهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, as cited by Abū Nuʿaym and also attributed to al-Farrāʾ, says the townspeople worshipped God alongside other gods, so the youths left idol worship but not worship of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r3.anchor: ذكر أبو نعيم الحافظ عن عطاء الخراساني أنهم كانوا يعبدون الله ويعبدون معه آلهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r4.claim: If the townspeople did not know or worship God, إلا الله is a disconnected exception because God was not among the objects they worshipped.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r4.anchor: ومنقطع إن كانوا لا يعرفون الله ولا يعبدونه لعدم اندراجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r5.claim: The wording وما يعبدون من دوننا in ʿAbd Allāh’s codex is explanatory gloss, not Qurʾān; it conflicts with the universally transmitted consonantal text وما يعبدون إلا الله.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r5.anchor: وما في مصحف عبد الله فيما ذكر هارون إنما أريد به تفسير المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r6.claim: An alternative makes وما يعبدون إلا الله a parenthetical divine statement that the youths worshipped no one but God, with إلا governed by an unrestricted exception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r6.anchor: وقيل: وما يعبدون إلا الله كلام معترض إخبار من الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r7.claim: فأووا means make the cave a refuge and remain there; their trust is that God will spread mercy and arrange their necessities, since He will not abandon those brought from disbelief to faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r7.anchor: فأووا إلى الكهف أي اجعلوه مأوى لكم تقيمون فيه وتأوون إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains يهيئ لكم as making the king’s threats easier and bringing ease, kindness, and comfort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ويهيئ لكم يسهل عليكم ما تخافون من الملك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī takes مرفقا to mean a replacement of their difficult situation with an easier one; the cited Zamzam verse illustrates بدلا, a substitute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: المعنى ويهيئ لكم بدلا من أمركم الصعب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r10.claim: The cited Zamzam line uses that water in place of another, illustrating Ibn al-Anbārī’s explanation of مرفقا as a substitute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150/r10.anchor: قال الشاعر: فليت لنا من ماء زمزم شربة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر والأعرج وشيبة وحميد وابن سعدان ونافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r1.claim: These readers pronounce مرفقا with an open mīm and kasra on fāʾ; other readers use a kasra mīm and open fāʾ, and both forms are reported for a facility and a bodily joint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والأعرج وشيبة وحميد وابن سعدان ونافع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says he knows only kasra on mīm for the practical facility, the hand joint, and every sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r2.anchor: لا أعرف في الأمر وفي اليد وفي كل شيء إلا كسر الميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī denies that the bodily joint is مرفق except with open mīm and kasra fāʾ; Abū Ḥātim disagrees, treating that form as a place noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r3.anchor: وأنكر الكسائي أن يكون المرفق من الجارحة إلا بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r4.claim: Abū Zayd analyzes مرفق as a verbal noun like رفق on the pattern مَفْعَل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: هو مصدر كالرفق جاء على مفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Hijaz speakers use open mīm and kasra fāʾ for a useful facility and reverse the vowels for the human joint; other Arabs may use kasra mīm for both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r5.anchor: أهل الحجاز يقولون مرفقا بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء فيما ارتفقت به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r6.speaker: معاذ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r6.claim: Muʿādh permits opening both mīm and fāʾ.

FARRA:v2p136#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p136#2/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p136#2/r1.claim: For مرفقا, al-A'mash and al-Hasan use kasra on م; Medina's readers and Asim use fatḥa. Most Arabs use kasra for both a human elbow and support in an affair, though both dialects occur.
FARRA:v2p136#2/r1.anchor: كسر الميم الأعمش والحسن، ونصبها أهل المدينة وعاصم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r1.claim: Their advice is to withdraw from the people and their worship, then worship God alone somewhere safe; its fulfillment confirms their sincerity and the preceding counsel.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r1.anchor: وإذا اجتنبتم عنهم وعما يعبدون فأخلصوا له العبادة في موضع تتمكنون منه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra takes faʾwu as the answer to idha; another analysis makes it evidence of an implied answer: first separate inwardly, then physically if needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r2.anchor: وإلى كون ( فأووا ( جواب إذ ذهب الفراء وقيل إنه دليل الجواب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r3.claim: Both conditional analyses are challenged because idha without ma is not conditional; the claim that it can be conditional is weak or merely semantic shorthand.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r3.anchor: واعترض كلا القولين بأن إذ بدون ما لا تكون للشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r4.claim: Accordingly, idha is causal or temporal, attached either to an implied command or to the stated command; Abu al-Baqa attaches it to an implied “they said to one another,” which the author calls astonishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r4.anchor: فهي هنا تعليلية أو ظرفية وتعلقها قيل بأووا محذوفا دل عليه المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r5.claim: A report from Qatada gives Ibn Masud's codex the explanatory wording “what they worship besides God”; Harun reports “besides us” in another codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود كما أخرج ابن جريج وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r6.speaker: في البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r6.claim: The codex variants are explanatory glosses, not readings, because they conflict with the Uthmanic consonantal text.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r6.anchor: وفي البحر أن المصحفين تفسير لا قراءة لمخالفته سواد الإمام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r7.claim: Yanshur means to spread and expand; rabb is the guardian who guided them to faith; mercy covers both worlds; yuhayyiʾ means to make easy, and the omitted object is good or similar benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r7.anchor: يبسط لكم ويوسع عليكم ( ﴿ ربكم ﴾ مالك أمركم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r8.claim: Min amrikum may attach to yuhayyiʾ as source or partitive, or, according to Ibn al-Anbari, mean God will replace their hard situation with a refuge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r8.anchor: على ما في بعض الحواشي متعلق بيهيء ومن الابتداء الغاية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reads min as substitution: God prepares a refuge in place of their difficult circumstances, as in the cited verse and a poem wishing for Zamzam water.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : للبدل والمعنى يهييء لكم بدلا عن أمركم الصعب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r10.claim: Min amrikum may alternatively be an implied circumstantial phrase modifying marfiqan.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r10.anchor: وجوز أن يكون حالا من ( مرفقا ) فيتعلق بمحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r11.claim: Putting lakum first signals early that the following provision benefits them and builds anticipation; their statement reflects trust, hope, and certainty in God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220#2/r11.anchor: وتقديم ( لكم ) لما مر مرارا من الايذان من أول الأمر بكون المؤخر من منافعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says every prophet was sent as a young man and every scholar received knowledge while young, citing Abraham, Moses, and the cave youths.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r1.anchor: أخرج الطبراني وابن المنذر عن ابن عباس قال : ما بعث الله تعالى نبيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r2.claim: The possibilities that a contemporary prophet told the youths their refuge would be prepared, or that one of them was a prophet receiving revelation, are unsupported conjecture.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r2.anchor: ولا يخفى أن ما ذكر مجرد احتمال من غير داع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r3.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, Humayd, Ibn Saʿdan, Nafiʿ, Ibn Amir, and others read marfiqan with mīm open and faʾ kasra; another reading reverses the vowels.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والأعرج وشيبة وحميد وابن سعدان ونافع وابن عامر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Thaʿlab say both vowel patterns mean either something useful or the bodily joint.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r4.anchor: ولا فرق بينه وبين ما هو بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء معنى على ما حكاه الزجاج وثعلب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r5.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r5.claim: Al-Farra says he knows only kasra for a useful object or the elbow; al-Kisai says the elbow alone takes the open-mim form, which Abu Hatim disputes as meaning a place.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r5.anchor: ونقل مكي عن الفراء أنه قال : لا أعرف في الأمر وفي اليد وفي كل شيء إلا كسر الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r6.claim: Other authorities call the two forms dialect variants for a useful thing, while distinguishing the elbow's form; Hejaz speakers and other Arabs differ, and Muadh permits both vowels open.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r6.anchor: وقيل : هما لغتان فيما يرتفق به وأما من اليد فبكسر الميم وفتح الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r7.claim: The verse supports migration to preserve religion and condemns remaining in an unbelieving land when remaining requires professing disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221/r7.anchor: هذا واستدل بالآية على حسن الهجرة لسلامة الدين وقبح المقام في دار الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r14.claim: Leaving the people and their worship symbolizes leaving the company of passion and turning away from everything besides God; taking refuge in the cave means retreating into solitude with the Beloved.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r14.anchor: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله ) أي وإذ خرجتم عن صحبة أهل الهوى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r15.speaker: بعض العارفين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r15.claim: A gnostic says solitude from everything besides God brings union with Him, which comes only after withdrawal; he compares this to the Prophet's retreat in Ḥirāʾ before revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r15.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : العزلة عن غير الله تعالى توجب الوصلة بالله عز وجل

MAJAZ:v1p394/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p394/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p394/r3.claim: Marfiqan means something used for comfort; some read marfaqan, while in the hand marfiq means elbow.
MAJAZ:v1p394/r3.anchor: «ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا» (16) هو ما ارتفق به ويقرؤه قوم مرفقا [فأما فى اليدين فهو مرفق] .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r7.claim: The youths tell one another to leave their people and everything they worship, except God, and seek the cave where God will spread mercy and provide ease.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r7.anchor: ثم قال بعضهم لبعض: {وإذ اعتزلتموهم} يعني قومهم (3) {وما يعبدون إلا الله}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r8.claim: He reads an explicit phrase, 'apart from God,' after what they worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r8.anchor: قرأ ابن مسعود "وما يعبدون من دون الله"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r9.claim: The common reading means they worshipped God as well as idols, so they had not abandoned God's worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r9.anchor: وأما القراءة المعروفة فمعناها: أنهم كانوا يعبدون الله ويعبدون معه الأوثان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r10.claim: They read marfiqan with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the fāʾ; others reverse the vowels, with the same sense of useful help.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p156/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر "مرفقا" بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء وقرأ الآخرون بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r5.claim: The youths address one another about abandoning the people and their idols; the exception may exclude worship of God, be a verbal noun meaning worship, or be a divine parenthesis affirming their monotheism.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r5.anchor: عطف على الضمير المنصوب، أي وإذا اعتزلتم القوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r6.claim: God's mercy includes expanded provision and benefit in both worlds; the youths speak confidently because of their firm trust in His favor.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r7.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r7.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read marfiqan with an a-vowel on the first syllable and an i-vowel on the second; the form is an anomalous verbal noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:14-18/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر { مرفقا } بفتح الميم

NAHHAS:v2p450/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p450/r3.claim: The opening ‘when you withdrew’ means ‘remember when you withdrew’; it is one youth speaking to the others.
NAHHAS:v2p450/r3.anchor: والتقدير اذكروا إذ اعتزلتموهم . هذا قول بعض الفتية لبعض

NAHHAS:v2p450/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p450/r4.claim: The object of ‘you withdrew from’ is what they worshipped; the exception excludes God, whom they did not abandon in worship.
NAHHAS:v2p450/r4.anchor: وما يعبدون ) ^ في موضع نصب أي واعتزلتم ما يعبدون فلم يعبدوه ^ ( إلا الله

NAHHAS:v2p450/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p450/r5.claim: ‘Then take refuge in the cave’ is answered by ‘your Lord will spread for you’.
NAHHAS:v2p450/r5.anchor: فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم ) ^ جواب الأمر

NAHHAS:v2p450/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
NAHHAS:v2p450/r6.claim: He knows only the kasra form marfiq for a matter, a hand, or anything else.
NAHHAS:v2p450/r6.anchor: زعم الأصمعي أنه لا يعرف في كلام العرب إلا مرفقا بكسر الميم في الأمر وفي اليد وفي كل شيء

NAHHAS:v2p450/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r7.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
NAHHAS:v2p450/r7.claim: They say the kasra is the fluent form, while the fatha is also allowed; the fatha distinguishes a facility from a human elbow.
NAHHAS:v2p450/r7.anchor: الكسائي والفراء أن اللغة الفصيحة كسر الميم ، وأن الفتح جائز . قال الفراء : وكان الذين فتحوا أرادوا أن يفرقوا بينه وبين مرفق الإنسان

NAHHAS:v2p450/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r8.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v2p450/r8.claim: He recognizes three good marfiq forms: one for a tool or facility, one patterned like masjid, and one meaning gentleness.
NAHHAS:v2p450/r8.anchor: فزعم الأخفش سعيد أن فيه ثلاث لغات جيدة مرفق ومرفق ومرفق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r1.claim: Since the youths lacked power against their numerous opponents, they migrated to preserve their faith after exposing their opponents' folly.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r1.anchor: وهم قوم لا يدان لهم بمقاومتهم , لكثرتهم وقلتهم , تسبب عن ذلك هجرتهم ليسلم لهم دينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r2.claim: Their separation from their people and their worship indicates that their community practiced polytheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r2.anchor: وهذا دليل على أنهم كانوا يشركون

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r3.claim: A possible interpretation is that they called the people's coerced submission to God's will and decrees a form of worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونوا سموا الانقياد كرها لمشيئته والخضوع بزعمهم لاقضيته عبادة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r4.claim: They take refuge in the cave because they have withdrawn from their people; God will extend enough mercy and prepare a useful comfort for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r4.anchor: فأوا } أي بسبب هذا الاعتزال , وهذا دليل العامل في { إذ

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r5.claim: Their hope rests on God's power to protect whoever seeks refuge in Him and trusts Him; He fulfills it by letting them sleep and raising them centuries later.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r5.anchor: فعلوا ذلك ففعل الله ما رجوه فيه , فجعل لهم أحسن مرفق بأن أنامهم ثم أقامهم بعد مضي قرون

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r6.claim: The reading مرفقا has kasra on mim and fatha on fa for most readers, but fatha on mim and kasra on fa for Nafi and Ibn Amir.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451/r6.anchor: وهو بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء في قراءة الجماعة , وبفتحها وكسر الفاء للنافع وابن عامر

DURR-FULL:v5p365/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r2.claim: The youths lived under an idolatrous tyrant who forced the people to worship idols; they left the city and God gathered them unexpectedly in the wilderness.
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r2.anchor: إنهم كانوا في مملكة ملك من الجبابرة يعبد الأوثان وقد أجبر الناس على عبادتها

DURR-FULL:v5p365/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r4.claim: When the youths' families reported them missing, the king predicted they would have a great destiny and recorded their names on a lead tablet kept in his treasury; this tablet was the Raqim.
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r4.anchor: فدعا بلوح من رصاص فكتب فيه أسماؤهم ثم طرح في خزانته فذلك قول الله: {أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم}

DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.claim: The sleepers were Muslim sons of kings who fled their people's religion and withdrew to the cave; they remained asleep until their people died and a Muslim generation arose under a Muslim king.
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: كان أصحاب الكهف أبناء ملوك رزقهم الله الإسلام

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r1.claim: After the youths disappeared, the king recorded their names on a lead tablet and put it in his treasury, saying they would have a great destiny; the tablet was the Raqim.
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r1.anchor: فقدوهم فخبروا الملك خبرهم فأمر بلوح من رصاص فكتب فيه أسماءهم وألقاه في خزانته

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r12.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r12.claim: The youths' people worshipped God along with many other gods; the youths abandoned worship of those deities but did not abandon worship of God.
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r12.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني في قوله: {وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله} قال: كان قوم الفتية يعبدون الله

DURR-FULL:v5p370/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r13.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r13.claim: Ibn Masud's codex reads من دون الله, clarifying that the youths withdrew from what their people worshipped apart from God.
DURR-FULL:v5p370/r13.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله} قال: هي في مصحف ابن مسعود: وما يعبدون من دون الله

DURR-FULL:v5p371/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r1.claim: The youths' cave lay between two mountains.
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فأووا إلى الكهف} قال: كان كهفهم بين جبلين

DURR-FULL:v5p371/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses مرفقا as food or provisions.
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r2.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا} يقول: عذاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r4.claim: The advice in verse 16 is best read as what they said to one another when they resolved to leave; if verse 14 means an audience with the king, an omitted 'some said to others' is needed here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r4.anchor: وبهذا يترجح أن قوله تعالى: إذ قاموا فقالوا إنما المراد به إذ عزموا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r5.claim: If the idolaters knew and revered God while associating idols with Him, 'except God' is a connected exception; if they knew only idols, it is disconnected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r5.anchor: فهو استثناء منقطع ليس من الأول، وإن فرضناهم يعرفون الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r6.claim: Qatada says Ibn Masud's wording 'what they worship besides God' explains the verse's phrase about what the people worship.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r7.speaker: هارون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r7.claim: Harun reports that some copies of Ibn Masud's codex read 'what they worship besides us.'
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r7.anchor: قال هارون وفي بعض مصاحفه «وما يعبدون من دوننا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r8.claim: The verse pictures their mutual counsel: having separated from the unbelievers, they would take refuge in the cave and rely on God to spread mercy and provide ease; the prayer concerns worldly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r8.anchor: ومضمن هذه الآية أن بعضهم قال لبعض إذ فارقنا الكفار وانفردنا بالله تعالى فلنجعل الكهف مأوى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r9.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r9.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read marfiqan with an open mīm and kasra on fāʾ; Abu Zayd calls this a verbal noun like rifq.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r9.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «مرفقا» بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r10.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي والحسن وطلحة والأعمش وابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r10.claim: These readers use the opposite vowels; both forms can mean ease or a bodily joint, though lexicographers disagree about which form denotes the joint.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p501/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي والحسن وطلحة والأعمش وابن أبي إسحاق «مرفقا»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r1.claim: Yamlīkha, the leader of the Companions of the Cave, says they have withdrawn from the idolaters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس هذا قول يمليخا وهو رئيس اصحاب الكهف قال لهم وإذ اعتزلتموهم أي فارقتموهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r2.speaker: عطاء الخراساني والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r2.claim: On one reading, they withdrew from the gods their people worshipped while continuing to worship God, whom the people also worshipped.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r3.claim: A second reading is that they withdrew from everything their people worshipped besides God; Abdullah's codex makes this wording explicit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r3.anchor: قال قتادة هي في مصحف عبد الله وما يعبدون من دون الله وهذا تفسيرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r4.claim: Taking refuge in the cave means making it their dwelling; God's spreading mercy includes expanding their provision.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r4.anchor: فأووا إلى الكهف أي اجعلوه مأواكم ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته أي يبسط عليكم من رزقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r5.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r5.claim: They read مرفقا with kasra on mīm and fatḥa on fāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي مرفقا بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r6.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r6.claim: They read مرفقا with fatḥa on mīm and kasra on fāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r6.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر مرفقا بفتح الميم وكسرالفاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r7.claim: The people of the Hijaz use the fatḥa-kasra form for any convenience one resorts to, while they use kasra for the human elbow; Arabs may use kasra for both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r7.anchor: قال الفراء أهل الحجاز يقولون مرفقا بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء في كل مرفق ارتفقت به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r8.claim: The phrase means God will provide a substitute for their difficult situation; a cited verse of poetry uses the same sense of substitute.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r8.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري معنى الآية ويهيئ لكم بدلا من أمركم الصعب مرفقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r9.claim: God would ease their fear of the king's oppression and bring them ease, gentleness, and kindness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p116/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس ويهيئ لكم يسهل عليكم ما تخافون من الملك وظلمه

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r1.claim: إذ اعتزلتموهم is governed by omitted speech, meaning someone told the others what to do when they separated.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r1.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r2.claim: Another analysis makes إذ causal (“because you withdrew”); the author rejects it.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r2.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r3.claim: If ما is relative, it means those worshipped, with an omitted object; إلا الله can be connected if they worshipped God and associates, or disconnected if only idols.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r3.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r4.claim: Under the relative parse, the report says they either worshipped God while associating others or worshipped only idols; the exception's antecedent may be ما or its object pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r4.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r5.claim: If ما is a مصدر particle, it means abandoning worship; إلا الله supplies omitted عبادة and has the same two exception options.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r5.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes ما as negative and the clause as God's parenthetical comment that they worship none but Him; إلا is free-standing.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r6.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa offers connected or disconnected exceptions under the negative reading; the author says his presentation wrongly ties both to that one reading.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r7.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r8.claim: Most read مرفقا with kasra ميم and fatḥa فاء; Nafi and Ibn Amir reverse the vowels.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r8.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r9.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r9.claim: One view says the two forms are synonymous for something leaned on, not a مصدر; another distinguishes a joint from a task.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r9.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r10.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r10.claim: Maki quotes al-Farra as knowing only kasra; the author says the mutawatir Nafi and Syrian readings disprove that.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r10.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r11.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r11.claim: Al-Kisa'i rejects kasra for the joint, recognizing only fatḥa, opposite al-Farra's report.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r11.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r12.claim: Al-Farra reports Hijaz usage with fatḥa-mim for aid and kasra for the elbow; other Arabs use kasra for both; Muadh allows both open as a مصدر.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16/r12.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف، أي: وقال بعضهم لبعض وقت اعتزالهم

SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r1.claim: من أمركم attaches to the preceding verb; من may mark origin or part.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r1.anchor: تواتر قراءة نافع والشاميين يرد عليه

SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari allows من to mean “instead of,” supported by a verse wishing for Zamzam water in place of something.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r2.anchor: تواتر قراءة نافع والشاميين يرد عليه

SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r3.claim: The phrase may be circumstantial to مرفقا with an omitted governor.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r3.anchor: تواتر قراءة نافع والشاميين يرد عليه

SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r4.speaker: الفَرّاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra's poem uses both forms for body joints; al-Zajjaj says both forms may denote a joint or aid.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r4.anchor: تواتر قراءة نافع والشاميين يرد عليه

SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم وأبو زيد
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r5.claim: Abu Hatim says fatḥa marks place; Abu Zayd calls it a مصدر on مفعل.
SAMIN-DURR:18:16#2/r5.anchor: تواتر قراءة نافع والشاميين يرد عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r3.claim: When persecution threatens faith, fleeing people is prescribed; a hadith describes a person's best property as sheep taken into the mountains to escape trials, but seclusion otherwise is not prescribed because it abandons communal prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r3.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث: "يوشك أن يكون خير مال أحدكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r4.claim: They left both the people and their religion, took refuge in the cave, and asked God to spread mercy over them and provide a comfortable arrangement.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r5.claim: The king could not find the fugitives; Ibn Kathir compares their concealment to Muhammad and Abu Bakr in the cave of Thawr, quoting the Prophet's reassurance and 9:40, while judging that story greater than the youths' cave.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p141/r6.claim: A report says the townspeople found the cave and sealed its entrance to kill the youths; Ibn Kathir doubts it because the next verse says sunlight reaches them morning and evening.

JISHUMI:v6p4363/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r5.claim: Iʿtizāl means withdrawal from an affair; the cited line uses it for keeping away from a house out of fear of enemies.
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r5.anchor: والعزل: التنحي عن الأمر، تقول: أنا بمعزل عن هذا الأمر، واعتزلت الأمر، قال الشاعر:

JISHUMI:v6p4363/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r6.claim: The Muʿtazila were so named because they left al-Ḥasan's circle after his death; another account says they rejected innovations and followed the early community.
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r6.anchor: وسمي عمرو بن عبيد وأصحابه معتزلة لما اعتزلوا حلقة الحسن بعد موته

JISHUMI:v6p4363/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r7.claim: Nashr is the opposite of folding: spreading a book, reviving the dead as though unfurled, or a pleasant wind spreading blessing.
JISHUMI:v6p4363/r7.anchor: والنشر: خلاف الطي، نشرت الكتاب، ونشر الله الميت أحياه بعد موته كأنه نشر بعد الطي،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r1.claim: The youths' words are one another's speech after their resolve to flee with their religion; wa-mā yaʿbudūn is coordinated with the attached pronoun, meaning they left their people and their objects of worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r1.anchor: { وإذ اعتزلتموهم } خطاب من بعضهم لبعض ، حين صممت عزيمتهم على الفرار بدينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r2.claim: The exception for God may be connected, since they acknowledged the Creator while associating others as Meccans did, or disconnected; alternatively, God interjects that the youths worshipped none but Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استثناء متصلا ، على ما روي : أنهم كانوا يقرون بالخالق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r3.claim: Marfiqan is read with fatḥa or kasra on the mīm and means something beneficial to rely upon.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r3.anchor: { مرفقا } قرىء ( بفتح الميم وكسرها ) وهو ما يرتفق به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r4.claim: Their confidence in finding relief may express trust and strong hope in God, or come from a prophet who told them, or from one of the youths being a prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#2/r4.anchor: إما أن يقولوا ذلك ثقة بفضل الله وقوة في رجائهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r8.claim: مرفقا may mean spacious ease or relief.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r9.claim: مرفقا may instead mean a livelihood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r9.anchor: مرفقا } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : سعة . الثاني : معاشا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r10.claim: A further possible sense of مرفقا is deliverance or rescue.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r11.claim: مرفقا is read with either kasra on mīm and fatḥa on fāʾ, or fatḥa on mīm and kasra on fāʾ; the former describes a benefit received, the latter one extended by you to another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p289/r11.anchor: ويقرأ { مرفقا } بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء { ومرفقا } بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء , والفرق بينهما أنه بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء إذا وصل إليك من غيرك , وبفتح الميم وكسر الفاء إذا وصل منك إلى غيرك

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r7.claim: The youths tell one another to leave their people and the idols worshipped besides God, while excepting God Himself from what they abandon.
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r7.anchor: ثم قال الفتية بعضهم لبعض، { وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون } ، من دون الله من الآلهة، ثم استثنوا، فقالوا: { إلا الله } ، فلا تعتزلوا معرفته،

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r8.claim: They do not abandon knowledge of God: they know He is their Lord and creator of them and all things.
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r8.anchor: فلا تعتزلوا معرفته، لأنهم عرفوا أن الله تعالى ربهم، وهو خلقهم وخلق الأشياء كلها،

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r9.claim: They take refuge in the cave; awā here means to go or reach a place, as also in 18:63.
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r9.anchor: يعني انتهوا إلى الكهف، كقوله سبحانه:

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r10.claim: God will spread mercy for them as provision, and prepare something that gives them ease; their sleep in the cave was that provision.
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r10.anchor: ينشر لكم } ، يعني يبسط لكم، { ربكم من رحمته } رزقا، { ويهيىء لكم من أمركم مرفقا } [آية: 16]،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r1.claim: The believers address one another after firmly resolving to flee with their religion; what they worship is grammatically coordinated to the pronoun, meaning abandon the people and their objects of worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r1.anchor: خطاب من بعضهم لبعض حيث صممت عزيمتهم على الفرار بدينهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r2.claim: The exception may be connected because the people acknowledged the Creator but associated partners; or disconnected, referring to unbelievers and their idols; alternatively, it is God's parenthetical report that the youths worshipped none but Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r2.anchor: استثناء متصل لأنهم كانوا يقرون بالخالق ويشركون معه غيره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r3.claim: They tell each other to make the cave their refuge; God will spread mercy, meaning provision, and prepare a useful means of ease.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r3.anchor: صيروا إليه واجعلوا الكهف مأواكم ﴿ ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ﴾ من رزقه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r4.speaker: المدني والشامي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r4.claim: The Madinan and Shami readings have marfiqan.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r5.claim: Their confidence and strong hope rest on trust in God and clear certainty; alternatively, a prophet of their time told them this.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6/r5.anchor: ثقة بفضل الله وقوة في رجائهم لتوكلهم عليه ونصوع يقينهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r1.claim: The words may be God's instruction to the youths or, in Ibn Atiyya's account, a speech by their leader Yemlikha.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r2.speaker: الغزنوي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r2.claim: Al-Ghaznawi instead names Maksalmina as their leader who urged retreat to the cave.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r2.anchor: قال لهم ذلك أي إذ اعتزلتموهم واعتزلتم ما يعبدون

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r3.claim: If the townspeople knew only idols and did not know God, illa Allah is a disjoint exception from what they worshipped.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r3.anchor: وهذا على تقدير إن الذين فر أهل الكهف منهم لا يعرفون الله

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r4.claim: If the townspeople knew God but associated idols with Him, the exception is connected because the youths left every object of worship except God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r4.anchor: وإن فرضنا أنهم يعرفون الله كما كانت العرب تفعل لكنهم يشركون أصنامهم

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r5.claim: The reading in Ibn Masud's codex, 'what they worship besides God,' is Qatada's explanatory gloss.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود «وما يعبدون من دون الله». قال قتادة هذا تفسيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r6.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r6.claim: Al-Khurasani says the youths came from a people worshipping God alongside idols, and they abandoned idol worship while keeping worship of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r6.anchor: كان فتية من قوم يعبدون الله ويعبدون معه آلهة

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r7.claim: On Qatada's reading, illa means 'other than' and ma is accusative, coordinated with the pronoun in 'you left them.'
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r7.anchor: فعلى ما قال قتادة تكون «إلا» بمنزلة غير

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r8.claim: The youths decide that after separating from unbelievers and their worship they will make the cave their refuge, trust God's mercy, and ask for a worldly convenience while secure about the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r8.anchor: فلنجعل الكهف مأوى ونتكل على الله فإنه سيبسط لنا رحمته

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r9.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the People of the Cave were polishers and names the cave Hayyum.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r9.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r10.claim: Mirfaq is read with mīm kasra or fatḥa and denotes something used for comfort; usage also distinguishes the arm joint from a place or matter of assistance.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:16/r10.anchor: قرىء بكسر الميم وفتحها، وهو ما يرتفق به

ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r2.claim: ما is accusative: if they leave their people and what they worship besides God, they will not abandon worship of Him; the cave becomes their refuge.
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r2.anchor: موضع (ما) نصب، المعنى إذا اعتزلتموهم واعتزلتم ما يعبدون إلا الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r3.claim: God spreads provision from His mercy and prepares an accommodation; both vowel patterns of مرفق are known, with kasra more common and better for the hand.
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r3.anchor: وذكر قطرب وغيره من أهل اللغة اللغتين جميعا في مرفق الأمر ومرفق اليد.

ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r4.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says he knows only the kasra-on-mīm, fatḥa-on-fāʾ pattern for مرفق.
ZAJJAJ:v3p272/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي: لا أعرف غير هدا.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.claim: The youths tell one another that withdrawing from the people and their objects of worship leaves their worship of God intact; they should make the cave their refuge.
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.anchor: اعتزلتم الشيء الذي يعبدونه إلا الله فإنكم لم تعتزلوا عبادة الله

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the cave command as the answer to idhā, like “when you do this, then do that”; it means go there and make it your abode.
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء هو جواب إذ كما تقول إذ فعلت كذا فافعل كذا

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.claim: God will spread His mercy over them and prepare ease in their affairs.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read marfaq with fatḥa on mīm and kasra on fāʾ; the others use kasra on mīm and fatḥa on fāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.anchor: قرأن افع وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية مرفقا بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ regards both marfaq pronunciations as dialect forms derived from irtifāq.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī accepts only the kasra-on-mīm reading for the body's elbow, while al-Farrāʾ accepts it for both the elbow and an affair.
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.anchor: وكان الكسائي ينكر في مرفق الإنسان الذي في اليد إلا كسر الميم

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.claim: Another explanation says both forms are dialects, with fatḥa more regular by analogy and kasra more common; marfaq can mean a means of support.
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.anchor: وقيل هما لغتان إلا أن الفتح أقيس والكسر أكثر

ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n19/r1.claim: Mirfaq means anything beneficial, concrete or abstract; here it is spiritual provision associated with abandoning the world and withdrawing into seclusion.
ASAD-NOTES:18:13#n19/r1.anchor: anything by which one benefits", whether concrete or abstract

STUDYQURAN:18:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r1.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r1.claim: The words are attributed to Tamlīkhā, also called Yamlīkhā or Iamblichus, the reported leader of the youths.
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r1.anchor: These are the words of Tamlīkhā (or Yamlīkhā, Iamblichus) the reported chief of the youths (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:18:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r2.claim: Tamlīkhā tells the youths to hide from disbelievers by taking refuge in the cave.
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r2.anchor: He instructs them to take refuge in the cave, to hide themselves from the disbelievers.

STUDYQURAN:18:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r3.claim: The youths’ retreat parallels the Prophet and Abū Bakr hiding in a cave during the Hijrah while fleeing the pursuing Makkans.
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r3.anchor: as they sought to elude the pursuing Makkans (see 9:40 and commentary; IK)

STUDYQURAN:18:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r4.claim: In both episodes the cave symbolizes the heart’s interior, providing miraculous sanctuary and refuge from worldly evils.
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r4.anchor: the cave, which is a symbol of the interior“space” of the heart, offers miraculous sanctuary

STUDYQURAN:18:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r5.claim: The promise of ease answers the youths’ prayer for sound judgment in their affair in verse 10.
STUDYQURAN:18:16/r5.anchor: suggests a response to the youths’ supplication to God in v. 10 that He make them incline to sound judgment in their affair.

TAB-FULL:v15p182/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r1.claim: The youths tell one another to leave their people, who worship gods besides God, and take refuge in the cave so that God may spread mercy and ease their situation.
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r1.anchor: وإذا اعتزلتم قومكم الذين يعبدون من الآلهة سوى الله

TAB-FULL:v15p182/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r2.claim: In the phrase about what their people worship, ma is accusative and coordinated with the pronoun suffix in iʿtazaltumuhum.
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r2.anchor: إذ كان ذلك معناه في موضع نصب عطفا لها على الهاء، والميم

TAB-FULL:v15p182/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r3.claim: Qatada notes that Abdullah's codex reads wa-ma yaʿbuduna min dun Allah, clarifying that the people worshipped other than God.
TAB-FULL:v15p182/r3.anchor: وهي في مصحف عبد الله: «وما يعبدون من دون الله» هذا تفسيرها

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r1.claim: Marfiqan means something by which the youths can find ease or support in their distress and fear for faith and life.

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra reports both vowel patterns for marfiq in the hand and in the sense of a useful thing.
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r2.anchor: وكان الفراء يحكي فيهما، أعني في مرفق الأمر واليد اللغتين كلتيهما

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r3.speaker: الكسائي
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i accepts only the pattern with fatha on fa and kasra on mim for the elbow.

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra reports both forms for the arm joint and for a beneficial thing, and cites a rajaz line using marfiq and mirfaq.
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r4.anchor: وكان الفراء يحكي فيهما، أعني في مرفق الأمر واليد اللغتين كلتيهما

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r5.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r5.claim: The rajaz poet's pairing of marfiq and mirfaq illustrates the two forms.

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r6.speaker: نحويي أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r6.claim: A Basran grammarian treats marfiqan as a noun meaning a useful thing, patterned like masjid, or as a form meaning ease.
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r6.anchor: شيئا ترتفقون به مثل المقطع، ومرفقا جعله اسما كالمسجد

TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r7.claim: Both regional readings are valid and equivalent, but he prefers the Iraqi kasra-mim, fatha-fa reading as the more eloquent and common Arabic form.
TAB-FULL:v15p182#2/r7.anchor: فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب. غير أن الأمر وإن كان كذلك

TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r1.claim: They most likely rose during an assembly enforcing idol worship, publicly declared monotheism, and fled under mortal threat; a report that six were the king's advisers supports this.

TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r2.claim: Public confession does not conflict with reports that they had concealed their faith: they could have practiced caution before suddenly declaring belief and leaving.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r2.anchor: ولا ينافي ذلك ما سيأتي من الروايات أنهم كانوا يسرون إيمانهم ويعملون بالتقية

TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r4.claim: Iʿtizāl is withdrawal, nashr is spreading, and mirfaq, with the cited vowelings, means gentle treatment or kind benefit.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r4.anchor: الاعتزال والتعزل التنحي عن أمر، والنشر البسط، والمرفق بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء وبالعكس وبفتحهما المعاملة بلطف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r5.claim: After leaving the people and their gods, they advise hiding in the cave, confident God will extend mercy and provide ease; these are the same gifts they requested on entering.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r5.anchor: وهذان اللذان تفرسوا بهما من نشر الرحمة وتهيئة المرفق هما اللذان سألوهما بعد دخول الكهف

TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r6.claim: The exception in “what they worship except God” is disconnected: the passage does not imply idolaters worshipped God alongside idols, contrary to other interpretations.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#8/r6.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله { وما يعبدون إلا الله } استثناء منقطع

TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r4.claim: Accounts differ on whether the ruler learned of their opposition before or after escape, whether they planned together or met by chance in the wilderness, and whether a shepherd or only his dog followed them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r4.anchor: وفي بعضها أنهم تواطؤوا على الخروج فخرجوا وفي بعضها أنهم خرجوا على غير معرفة من بعضهم لحال بعض

TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r5.claim: Some reports say the ruler searched unsuccessfully, others found them asleep and walled up the cave until a shepherd broke in; still others say they met the king and died, or died before his arrival and were hidden, after which a mosque was built.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#28/r5.anchor: فأمر أن يبنى على باب الكهف بنيان ليحتبسوا فيموتوا جوعا وعطشا جزاء لعصيانهم

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r5.claim: Al-Sadiq says they concealed belief and outwardly showed disbelief, so God rewarded them twice; other reports say they wore zunnar belts and attended festivals.
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r5.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن أصحاب الكهف أسروا الإيمان وأظهروا الكفر

TABATABAI:18:26#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r6.claim: The youths’ departure was migration from a society that prevented open monotheism and threatened stoning or forced conversion; their declaration at some point does not rule out taqiyya earlier.
TABATABAI:18:26#4/r6.anchor: ولا يرد عليه أن ظاهر قوله تعالى حكاية عنهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r1.claim: Their coordinated flight and abandonment of family, property, and homeland showed opposition, but their first declaration can be understood as private resolve rather than public defiance; either way, the verses allow taqiyya earlier.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r1.anchor: فقد كانوا على خطر عظيم لو ظهر عليهم القوم ولم ينته أمرهم إلا إلى أحد أمرين الرجم أو الدخول في ملة القوم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r2.claim: A report says they left without knowing one another’s faith or arranging a meeting, exchanged pledges in the wilderness, then disclosed and found they shared one belief.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي أيضا عن أبي بكر الحضرمي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال خرج أصحاب الكهف على غير معرفة ولا ميعاد

TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the youths left separately from an idolatrous city and cautiously questioned one another before making pledges, agreeing that God alone is Lord and seeking refuge in the cave.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#29/r4.anchor: فبلغ ذلك ابن عباس فأنشأ يحدث عنهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.claim: The cave story circulated in detailed reports from al-Qummī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, Ibn Isḥāq, Wahb ibn Munabbih, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, among others.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#32/r10.anchor: وردت قصة الكهف مفصلة كاملة في عدة روايات عن الصحابة والتابعين وأئمه أهل البيت

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.claim: The transmitted accounts disagree even on major features, while reports about dates, rulers, lineage, appearance, names, and the title أصحاب الرقيم diverge still more.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r1.anchor: من الاختلاف في متونها بحيث لا تكاد تتفق في جهة بارزه من جهات القصة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.claim: One cause is the story’s prominence among People of the Book: Quraysh learned it from them, and its Christian images and monuments spread it widely, so communities reshaped it to fit their beliefs.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r2.anchor: أن القصة مما اعتنت به أهل الكتاب كما يستفاد من رواياتها أن قريشا تلقتها عنهم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.claim: A second cause is Muslims’ broad collection of outside reports, especially through converts such as Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; later transmitters treated such material as prophetic reports.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r3.anchor: اختلط بهم قوم من علماء أهل الكتاب دخلوا في الإسلام كوهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.claim: The Qurʾān selects key lessons that serve guidance instead of supplying a complete historical account; it is a book of guidance, not history.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r4.anchor: فما كتاب الله بكتاب تاريخ وإنما هو كتاب هدى

TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.claim: The Qurʾānic narrative first shows the youths’ truth-bearing withdrawal and long sleep, then their awakening and exchange that exposes them, and finally their discovery and the mosque built over them.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#33/r5.anchor: أورد أولا شطرا من محاورتهم يشير إلى معنى قيامهم لله وثباتهم على كلمة الحق

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.claim: The Qurʾān omits names, ancestry, birth, upbringing, occupations, social standing, dates, rulers, cities, persecutors, and the dog’s identity because guidance does not depend on them; historians and early exegetes filled these gaps, producing divergent accounts.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r1.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من الأمور التي لا يتوقف غرض الهداية على العلم بشيء منها كما يتوقف عليه غرض البحث التاريخي

TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r3.claim: Seeing that remaining would force them to conceal truth or conform to idolatry, the youths chose to affirm God as Lord of heaven and earth, reject other gods as false, and withdraw to the cave trusting in divine mercy and guidance.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#34/r3.anchor: علموا أن سبيلهم أن يقوموا على التوحيد ورفض الشرك ثم اعتزال القوم

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.speaker: أهل الرواية والتاريخ
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.claim: Most historians date the story between Jesus and Muḥammad; it is absent from the two Testaments, though some Muslim reports say Quraysh heard it from Jews, while Christians preserved it extensively.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r1.anchor: معظم أهل الرواية والتاريخ على أن القصة وقعت في الفترة بين النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وبين المسيح

TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.claim: Christian accounts resemble Ibn Isḥāq’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās in some respects but differ from Muslims on the number of sleepers, whether they had a dog, and the length of their sleep.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#36/r2.anchor: أن المصادر السريانية تذكر عدد أصحاب الكهف ثمانية في حين يذكره المسلمون

TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.claim: After centuries as a ruined, forgotten site, Jordanian excavation uncovered Rujayb; the author considers its archaeological signs and some Muslim reports the strongest fit for the Qurʾānic cave.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#38/r4.anchor: وقامت عدة من الأمارات والشواهد الأثرية على كونه هو كهف أصحاب الكهف المذكورين في القرآن

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.claim: Amman stands on the site of Philadelphia, a major and beautiful city before Islam that remained under Roman control from the early second century until the Muslim conquest.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r1.anchor: كانت هي وما والاها تحت استيلاء الروم منذ أوائل القرن الثاني الميلادي حتى فتح المسلمون الأرض المقدسة

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.claim: Other proposed locations include a cave on Mount Qāsiyūn near Damascus, one at Petra, a Scandinavian cave with seven uncorrupted Roman-looking bodies, and a cave near Nakhchivan.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r2.anchor: والكهف الثالث كهف بجبل قاسيون بالقرب من الصالحية بدمشق الشام

TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.claim: No evidence identifies any proposed cave as the Qurʾānic one; the Scandinavian and Caucasus claims conflict with the story’s Roman setting and the limits of Roman power.
TABATABAI:18:9-26#39/r3.anchor: ولا شاهد يشهد على كون شيء من هذه الكهوف هو الكهف المذكور في القرآن الكريم

TABRISI:18:13-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:13-14/r1.claim: For marfiqan, people of Medina, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Aʿshā, and al-Barjamī from Abū Bakr read fatḥa on mīm and kasra on fāʾ; the other readers reverse those vowels.
TABRISI:18:13-14/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر والأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر مرفقا بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

TABRISI:18:13-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r2.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:18:13-14/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj and Quṭrub acknowledge both vowel forms for ‘benefit/support’ and ‘joint’; kasra on the arm-joint form is more idiomatic.
TABRISI:18:13-14/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج وذكر قطرب وغيره اللغتين جميعا في مرفق الأمر ومرفق اليد

TABRISI:18:13-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:18:13-14/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says the fatḥa form means a thing used for benefit, while the kasra form is a noun; it may be a dialect or a verbal noun form.
TABRISI:18:13-14/r3.anchor: قال أبو الحسن مرفقا أي شيئا يرتفقون به مثل المقطع ونحوه ومرفقا جعله اسما

TABRISI:18:13-14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:13-14/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:13-14/r5.claim: Iʿtizāl means withdrawing or distancing oneself; a line of poetry uses taʿazzul for withdrawal, and the name Muʿtazila was applied to ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd’s circle because they left al-Ḥasan’s gathering.
TABRISI:18:13-14/r5.anchor: والاعتزال التنحي عن الأمر والتعزل بمعناه

TABRISI:18:15-16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:15-16/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:15-16/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Tamlikhā, the youths’ leader, spoke: if they left their people and idols, they would still not abandon worship of God.
TABRISI:18:15-16/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس وهذا من قول تمليخا وهو رئيس أصحاب الكهف قال لهم فإذا فارقتموهم

TABRISI:18:15-16/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:15-16/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:15-16/r4.claim: If some youths worshiped God alongside the idols, the exception ‘except God’ is connected; if all worshiped only idols, it is a disconnected exception.
TABRISI:18:15-16/r4.anchor: الاستثناء متصلا ويجوز أن يكون جميعهم

TABRISI:18:15-16/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:15-16/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:15-16/r5.claim: They should make the cave their refuge; God will spread mercy and arrange ease, gentleness, and what they need for their livelihood.

TABRISI:18:15-16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:15-16/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:15-16/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the arrangement as God making their fear of the ruler and his injustice easy to bear, with gentleness and relief.
TABRISI:18:15-16/r6.anchor: ويسهل عليكم ما تخافون من الملك وظلمه ويأتيكم باليسر والرفق واللطف عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:18:15-16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:15-16/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:15-16/r7.claim: The passage shows the high status of migration for religion and the wrongness of staying in an unbelieving land when remaining requires professing disbelief.
TABRISI:18:15-16/r7.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على عظم منزلة الهجرة في الدين وعلى قبح المقام في دار الكفر

THALABI:v6p147#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p147#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p147#2/r6.claim: Fearing Daqyanus's return, the youths decide to take household provisions, give some away, and retreat to a nearby cave to worship God.
THALABI:v6p147#2/r6.anchor: فائتمروا بينهم أن يأخذ كل رجل نفقة من بيت أبيه فيتصدقوا بها

THALABI:v6p148/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p148/r1.claim: The youths take their remaining provisions to the cave, and their dog follows them.
THALABI:v6p148/r1.anchor: وانطلقوا بما بقي معهم من نفقتهم، وأتبعهم كلب كان لهم

THALABI:v6p148/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r2.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v6p148/r2.claim: Ka'b relates that a dog repeatedly follows them, says it loves God's beloved, and offers to guard them while they sleep.
THALABI:v6p148/r2.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: مروا بكلب فنبح عليهم فطردوه، فعاد ففعلوا ذلك مرارا

THALABI:v6p148/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p148/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says seven youths flee Daqyanus by night when he summons them to worship idols; a believing shepherd and his dog join them.
THALABI:v6p148/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هربوا ليلا من دقيانوس بن جلانوس حيث دعاهم إلى عبادة الأصنام

THALABI:v6p148/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p148/r4.claim: The youths live in the cave praying and praising God, while Tamlikha secretly buys food and checks whether the ruler has mentioned them.
THALABI:v6p148/r4.anchor: فلبثوا فيه ليس لهم عمل إلا الصلاة والتسبيح والتكبير والتحميد ابتغاء وجه الله تعالى

THALABI:v6p148/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p148/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p148/r5.claim: Tamlikha disguises himself in poor clothing when entering the city to buy their food and hear the news.
THALABI:v6p148/r5.anchor: ثم يأخذ ورقة فينطلق إلى المدينة فيشتري طعاما وشرابا ويسمع ويتجسس لهم الخبر

THALABI:v6p149/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p149/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p149/r1.claim: The youths' parents say their sons spent the money in the city and withdrew to Mount Yanjalus; the ruler releases the parents.
THALABI:v6p149/r1.anchor: ذهبوا بأموالنا وأهلكوها في أسواق المدينة ثم انطلقوا فارتقوا إلى جبل يدعى ينجلوس

THALABI:v6p150/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p150/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
