THALABI:v6p150/r1.claim: The youths find a nearby cave and enter with a hunting dog, saying God will spread mercy and provide a suitable way forward; they sleep 309 years.
THALABI:v6p150/r1.anchor: فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

THALABI:v6p150/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p150/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v6p150/r5.claim: The pursued young believers escape with a fellow believer working in a field and his dog, reach a cave at night, and sleep there by God's act.
THALABI:v6p150/r5.anchor: فمروا بصاحب لهم في زرع وهو على مثل إيمانهم فذكروا له أنهم التمسوا

THALABI:v6p158/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r15.claim: The youths urge one another to leave their people and the idols they worship besides God, then take refuge in the cave.
THALABI:v6p158/r15.anchor: يعني قومكم وما يعبدون إلا الله، أي واعتزلتم أصنامهم التي يعبدونها من دون الله

THALABI:v6p158/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r16.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v6p158/r16.claim: The codex of Abdullah ibn Masud adds 'besides God' after the phrase about what the people worship.
THALABI:v6p158/r16.anchor: وكذلك هو في مصحف عبد الله: (وما يعبدون من دون الله)

THALABI:v6p158/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r17.claim: They are told to go to the cave; God will extend mercy and arrange a comfortable provision or resource for them.
THALABI:v6p158/r17.anchor: ينشر، أي يبسط لكم ويظهر لكم ربكم من رحمته

THALABI:v6p158/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p158/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p158/r18.claim: The word marfiqan means something a person uses for comfort or support, and has two vocalized forms.
THALABI:v6p158/r18.anchor: والمرفق: ما يرتفق به الإنسان، وفيه لغتان: مرفق، ومرفق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r1.claim: He parses the command to take refuge in the cave as the response to idh, like an if-then construction; it means make the cave your home.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: (هذا جواب "إذ" كما تقول: إذ فعلت كذا فافعل كذا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r2.claim: Yanshur means that God will spread His mercy over the youths.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r2.anchor: {ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته} أي: يبسطها عليكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r3.claim: He says God will ease their fear of the king and his oppression, bringing them relief, kindness, and gentleness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يسهل عليكم ما خوفكم من الملك وظلمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r4.claim: He understands the promised mرفق as breakfast or food.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r5.claim: Others gloss mرفق as an exit; in general it is anything by which one gets help or comfort.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r5.anchor: وكل ما ارتفقت به فهو مرفق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r6.claim: The word has variants mرفق and مرفق in both the sense of a useful matter and the body's elbow; Medinan readers use the open-mim form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r6.anchor: ويقال فيه أيضا: مرفق بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء، كقراءة أهل المدينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r7.claim: He defines mرفق as what one uses for support, distinguishing the body's joint as mرفق.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: (المرفق: ما ارتفقت به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r8.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r8.claim: He glosses mرفقا as a thing they can use, like maqṭaʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r8.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ({مرفقا} أي: شيئا يرتفقون به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r9.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r9.claim: He explains the kasra reading as a lexicalized noun rather than a regular place or verbal noun; the open form can be a dialect variant of the verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي: (قوله: جعله اسما، أي: جعل المرفق اسما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r10.claim: Most Arabs use kasra in both the word for a helpful matter and the elbow, though some use fatha for both; the opening may distinguish the elbow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: (وأكثر العرب على كسر الميم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r11.speaker: يونس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r11.claim: He prefers kasra for a useful matter and fatha for the elbow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r11.anchor: وقال يونس: (الذي أختار المرفق في الأمر، والمرفق في اليد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r12.speaker: الأصمعي وقطرب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r12.claim: Al-Asmaʿi recognizes only kasra for both senses, while Qutrub reports both pronunciations for both.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p548/r12.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: (لا أعرف إلا الكسر فيهما)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r5.claim: Temlikha, their leader, urged the youths to separate from their people and idols while continuing to worship God, then retreat to the cave for mercy and food.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r5.anchor: فزعم أن معه إلها، فقال لهم تمليخا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:13-16/r6.claim: God would spread his mercy over them and arrange an easy source of food.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r6.claim: The youths tell one another to withdraw from their people and take refuge in the cave, trusting God to extend mercy and prepare ease for them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r7.claim: Qatāda says the codex of ʿAbd Allāh reads 'what they worship besides God', which explains the wording.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174/r7.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: هي في مصحف عبد الله: وما يعبدون من دون الله. وهذا تفسيرها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r1.claim: The youths reach the cave; God will spread His mercy for them, meaning widen it, and arrange a useful refuge.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r1.anchor: {فأووا إلى الكهف} [الكهف: 16] ، يعني: فانتهوا إلى الكهف.

ELMALILI:18:15-18/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:15-18/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:15-18/r6.claim: The youths expect their retreat to bring God's mercy and ease; the light of faith ultimately leads to the mercy of the All-Merciful and success in their aim.
ELMALILI:18:15-18/r6.anchor: zira nûr-i imanın âkıbet rahmet-i Rahmân’a kavuşturacağı muhakkaktır

ELMALILI:18:15-18/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:15-18/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:15-18/r7.claim: Their prayer to receive mercy and right guidance was followed by God putting them to sleep, either to shield them from oppressors' distress or after the cave entrance was walled.
ELMALILI:18:15-18/r7.anchor: kulaklarının üzerine vurulup yani o zâlimler tarafından bir keder işitilmemek için yatırılıp veyahut mağaranın kapısına bir binâ kurdurulup senelerce uyutuldular

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.claim: Unable to profess or practice monotheism safely amid persecution, the youths left their people with their dog and sought refuge in the cave.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r1.anchor: imanlarını serbestçe ifade etme ve inançlarının gereğini yerine getirme imkânı bulamayacaklarını, hatta onların arasında hayat hakkına dahi sahip olamayacaklarını anlayınca, köpeklerini de yanlarına alarak mağaraya sığındılar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.claim: They prayed for mercy and a way out, hoping for God’s help; God accepted their prayer and caused them to sleep deeply for a long time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:13/r2.anchor: Allah’ın yardımını ve bir kurtuluş yolu göstereceğini ümit ederek, “Rabbimiz! Bize rahmet et ve bize bir çıkış yolu hazırla!” diye dua ettiler.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Marfaq means something useful to a person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The account suppresses the escalating conflict: imminent stoning led the youths to the cave they had chosen, where God assured them of mercy and provision if they took the initiative to leave their people and idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the danger of stoning them to death looked imminent, as is evident from verse 20

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: When servants fear God and set out toward Him, He provides the means they need, as also taught in al-Talaq.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is stated thus in verses 2-3 of Sūrah al-Ṭalāq

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The guidance to seek refuge is a particular kind of divine inspiration, comparable to God's instruction to Moses' mother to place him in a box and set him afloat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this is a particular type of divine revelation and is similar to the one sent to Moses’ mother

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the Sufi inference that this verse praises world-isolation: the youths fled mortal persecution, as the Prophet once sought refuge in Thawr, rather than pursuing monasticism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: These people had not adopted this life of isolation because of any inclination towards monasticism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Against exegetes who treat the promise of mercy and provision as the youths' own speech, Islahi says its certainty marks it as God's promise; a humble person could voice it only as prayer or yearning, as in verse 10.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: constitutes the promise of divine help cannot be stated by a humble individual

ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r8.claim: A report cited in Majmaʿ al-Bayān says Yamlikha was the speaker addressing the youths about withdrawing from their people and their worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r8.anchor: وفي مجمع البيان عن ابن عباس أن قائله يمليخا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r9.claim: Iʿtizāl means physical or inward avoidance; ma may be relative or infinitival, and on either reading the exception can be connected, with an implied noun needed for one infinitival construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r9.anchor: والاعتزال تجنب الشيء بالبدن أو بالقلب وكلا الأمرين محتمل هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r10.claim: The youths' phrase about withdrawing can be read as relative or infinitival; if infinitival, an implied act of worship is needed for the exception to remain connected.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن الاستثناء فيهما متصل ويقدر على الاحتمال الثاني مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r11.claim: The exception may instead be disconnected; under one reading the townspeople worship Allah along with other gods, while the alternative says they worship only others, which better fits 18:15.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون منقطعا وعلى الأول يكون القوم عابدين الله تعالى وعابدين غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r12.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r12.claim: A report from Ata al-Khurasani says the youths' people worshipped Allah and various other gods, and the youths abandoned the idols but not worship of Allah.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r12.anchor: أخرج سعيد بن منصور وابن أبي حاتم وأبو نعيم عن عطاء الخراساني أنه قال : كان قوم الفتية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r13.claim: The poem about ʿAtika's house illustrates iʿtizāl, avoiding something by body or heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p219#2/r13.anchor: يا بيت عاتكة الذي أتغزل حذر العدى وبه الفؤاد موكل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p220/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220/r1.claim: A further parsing makes mā negative with an unrestricted exception: God inserts the youths' monotheistic declaration parenthetically between 'when you withdraw' and 'take refuge in the cave'; al-Kashf explains the parenthesis by the following clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p220/r1.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما نافية والاستثناء مفرغ والجملة إخبار من الله تعالى عن الفتية بالتوحيد

AKHFASH:v2p428/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p428/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p428/r3.claim: مرفقا denotes something useful for comfort; it can be a noun like المسجد, a dialectal form from رفق يرفق, or a variant intended as رفق.
AKHFASH:v2p428/r3.anchor: وقال {من أمركم مرفقا} أي: شيئا يرتفقون به مثل: "المقطع" و {مرفقا} جعله اسما ك"المسجد"

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p224/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p224/r1.claim: Mirfaq with kasra on mīm derives from irtifāq, finding rest; with fatḥa it refers to the hand; the author also allows both as eloquent dialect forms.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p224/r1.anchor: بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء وبفتح الميم وكسر الفاء فالحجة لمن كسر الميم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī kasra mīm and open fāʾ in mirfaq; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir open mīm and kasra fāʾ, also reported from al-Kisāʾī via Abū Bakr.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p388/r2.anchor: 2 واختلفوا فى فتح الميم وكسر الفاء وكسر الميم وفتح الفاء من قوله ﴿ مرفقا ﴾ 16

NASHR:v2p310/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r6.speaker: المدنيان وابن عامر
NASHR:v2p310/r6.claim: The two Medinese readers and Ibn ʿAmir open the mim and kasr the fa in mirfaqan.
NASHR:v2p310/r6.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وابن عامر بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء

NASHR:v2p310/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r7.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p310/r7.claim: The other readers kasr the mim and open the fa in mirfaqan.
NASHR:v2p310/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء

NASHR:v1p447/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p447/r2.speaker: الغازي بن قيس
NASHR:v1p447/r2.claim: Al-Ghazi ibn Qays records some codices drawing the hamza as alif in hayyiʾ and yuhayyiʾ, avoiding excessive deletion where a preceding ya is doubled; he reports the same spelling for two other phrases.
NASHR:v1p447/r2.anchor: نص على تصويرها ألفا فيهما وفي (ومكر السيئ والمكر السيئ) الغازي بن قيس في هجاء السنة له

NASHR:v1p447/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p447/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p447/r3.claim: Al-Dani rejects writing the hamza as alif, calling that spelling contrary to consensus.
NASHR:v1p447/r3.anchor: أنكر الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني كتابة ذلك بألف، وقال: إنه خلاف الإجماع

NASHR:v1p447/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p447/r4.speaker: السخاوي
NASHR:v1p447/r4.claim: Al-Sakhawi says al-Dani lacked certainty and knowledge of the Syrian codex, where the spellings described by al-Ghazi occur.
NASHR:v1p447/r4.anchor: وقال السخاوي: إن ذلك لم يقله أبو عمرو، عن يقين، بل عن غلبة ظن وعدم اطلاع

NASHR:v1p447/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p447/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p447/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says he personally saw those forms in the Syrian codex; al-Shatibi and others instead specify two ya letters in the written form.
NASHR:v1p447/r5.anchor: وقد رأيت هذه المواضع في المصحف الشامي كما ذكره الغازي بن قيس

NASHR:v1p447/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p447/r6.speaker: الشاطبي
NASHR:v1p447/r6.claim: Al-Shatibi and others specify that hayyiʾ and yuhayyiʾ are written with two ya letters.
NASHR:v1p447/r6.anchor: وقد نص الشاطبي وغيره على رسم (هيئ ويهيئ) بياءين

NASHR:v1p465/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r1.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p465/r1.claim: Some readers distinguish by the hamza's written seat: when it is written as waw or ya they use eased rūm, but when written as alif they substitute according to the codex spelling.
NASHR:v1p465/r1.anchor: فما صورت الهمزة فيه رسما واوا أو ياء وقف عليه بالروم بين بين، وما صورت فيه ألفا وقف عليه بالبدل اتباعا للرسم

NASHR:v1p465/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r2.speaker: أبو محمد مكي وأبو عبد الله بن شريح
NASHR:v1p465/r2.claim: Makki and Ibn Shurayḥ choose that written-seat distinction for stopping on hamza.
NASHR:v1p465/r2.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي محمد مكي وأبي عبد الله بن شريح

NASHR:v1p465/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r4.speaker: أبو علي بن بليمة
NASHR:v1p465/r4.claim: Ibn Balima applies eased rūm after an alif but not after a moving letter.
NASHR:v1p465/r4.anchor: وانفرد أبو علي بن بليمة بالروم كذلك فيما وقعت الهمزة فيه بعد الألف دون ما وقع فيه بعد متحرك

NASHR:v1p465/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم بن الفحام
NASHR:v1p465/r5.claim: Ibn al-Faḥḥām extends the rūm practice across all three hamza vowels and allows either face after a moving letter for damma and kasra.
NASHR:v1p465/r5.anchor: ووافقه على ذلك أبو القاسم بن الفحام، إلا أنه أطلقه في الأحوال الثلاث ضما وفتحا وكسرا من غير خلاف

NASHR:v1p465/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r6.speaker: ابن سوار
NASHR:v1p465/r6.claim: Ibn Sawwar agrees with this practice for hamza following an alif.
NASHR:v1p465/r6.anchor: ووافقه ابن سوار فيما كان بعد الألف

NASHR:v1p465/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r7.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p465/r7.claim: Some anomalously allow eased rūm in all three vowel states, both after alif and after other letters, without distinguishing fatha.
NASHR:v1p465/r7.anchor: وشذ بعضهم وأجاز الروم بالتسهيل في الحركات الثلاث بعد الألف وغيرها ولم يفرق بين المفتوح وغيره

NASHR:v1p465/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p465/r8.claim: Al-Dani records this anomalous option in his Jamiʿ but does not say he received it from any reader.
NASHR:v1p465/r8.anchor: وحكاه الحافظ أبو عمرو في جامعه، ولم يذكر أنه قرأ به على أحد

NASHR:v1p465/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون
NASHR:v1p465/r9.claim: Ibn Ghalbun mentions the option in his Tadhkira but does not approve it, and his transmitted text from Ḥamza is questionable.
NASHR:v1p465/r9.anchor: وأبو الحسن طاهر بن غلبون في تذكرته ولم يرضه، وحكى نصا لحمزة وفيه نظر

NASHR:v1p465/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p465/r10.claim: When a hamza is obligatorily sukun and substituted with a long-vowel letter, the substitute remains intact and is not altered by jussive syntax.
NASHR:v1p465/r10.anchor: إذا كانت الهمزة ساكنة لموجب فأبدلت حرف مد بقي ذلك الحرف بحاله لا يؤثر فيه الجازم

NASHR:v1p465/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p465/r12.claim: When stopping by substitution on a final hamza after alif, two alifs meet; one may be deleted for the meeting of sukuns or both retained because pause permits it.
NASHR:v1p465/r12.anchor: فإنه يجتمع ألفان، فإما أن تحذف إحداهما للساكنين أو تبقيهما

NASHR:v1p465/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p465/r13.claim: If the first alif is considered deleted, only shortness results; if the second is deleted, both long and short measures are possible because the cause has changed.
NASHR:v1p465/r13.anchor: فإن قدرتها الأولى فالقصر ليس إلا لفقد الشرط، إلا أن الألف تكون مبدلة من همزة ساكنة

NASHR:v1p465/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p465/r14.speaker: أبو محمد مكي
NASHR:v1p465/r14.claim: Makki's Taysir discussion deletes one alif and permits long measure when the second is deleted, short when the first is deleted; other cited authorities allow a medium measure when both remain.
NASHR:v1p465/r14.anchor: فنص مكي في " التبصرة " على حذف أحد الألفين

NASHR:v1p469/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p469/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p469/r2.claim: For forms such as hayyiʾ, yuhayyiʾ, nabbiʾ, iqraʾ, and nashaʾ, a proposed full articulation at pause is invalid under the preceding rule, as is deleting the substituted long-vowel letter for jussive syntax.
NASHR:v1p469/r2.anchor: ووجه ثالث في (هيئ ويهيئ ونبئ واقرأ ونشاء) ونحوه، وهو التحقيق

NASHR:v1p469/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p469/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p469/r7.claim: For a damma hamza after kasra in yunsʾi and similar forms, five stop faces are cited: silent ya substitution, ya with damma attributed to al-Akhfash, rūm or ishām, easing toward waw on rūm per Sibawayh, and an exceptional easing toward ya on rūm.

NASHR:v2p103/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p103/r1.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v2p103/r1.claim: Readers unanimously use tafkhim for rāʾ after damma and for rāʾ after kasra when an istiʿla letter follows; a report of tarqiq for Warsh through al-Azraq in such cases is an error.
NASHR:v2p103/r1.anchor: فإن وقع بعدها حرف استعلاء فلا خلاف في تفخيمها من أجل حرف الاستعلاء

NASHR:v2p103/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p103/r2.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v2p103/r2.claim: Some wrongly attribute tarqiq after an istiʿla letter to Warsh through al-Azraq; Ibn al-Jazari says the correct practice is unanimous tafkhim.
NASHR:v2p103/r2.anchor: وقد شذ بعضهم فحكى ترقيق ما وقع بعد حرف استعلاء من ذلك عن ورش من طريق الأزرق

NASHR:v2p103/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p103/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p103/r8.claim: Some authorities thicken the ra when the mim is kasra-voweled, treating its kasra as incidental; Ibn al-Jazari prefers tarqiq because the kasra is necessary, even though the mim is added.
NASHR:v2p103/r8.anchor: والصواب فيه الترقيق وأن الكسرة فيه لازمة وإن كانت الميم زائدة كما سيأتي

NASHR:v2p107/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p107/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p107/r4.claim: A kasra is necessary when it belongs to an original letter or one whose removal damages the word; another view calls any kasra on an added letter incidental.
NASHR:v2p107/r4.anchor: فاللازمة ما كانت على حرف أصلي، أو منزل منزلة الأصلي يخل إسقاطه بالكلمة والعارضة بخلاف ذلك

NASHR:v2p107/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p107/r5.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v2p107/r5.claim: For readers who kasr the mim and open the fa in mirfaqan, necessary-versus-incidental classification determines tarqiq versus tafkhim; Ibn al-Jazari prefers necessary kasra and tarqiq, analogizing to Warsh's tarqiq in al-miḥrāb and ikhrājan.
NASHR:v2p107/r5.anchor: فعلى الأول تكون لازمة فترقق الراء معها، وعلى الثاني تكون عارضة فتفخم والأول هو الصواب

NASHR:v2p107/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p107/r6.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v2p107/r6.claim: Most treat tafkhim as the ra's default and allow tarqiq only when a cause exists; Makki argues that every non-kasra ra can be thickened but not every ra can be thinned.
NASHR:v2p107/r6.anchor: فذهب الجمهور إلى الأول واحتج له مكي فقال: إن كل راء غير مكسورة فتغليظها جائز وليس كل راء فيها الترقيق

NASHR:v2p107/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p107/r7.speaker: غيره
NASHR:v2p107/r7.claim: Other authorities argue that ra is neutral between thick and thin, citing its tongue position near the upper palate and its strong repetition, which makes its vowel quality especially forceful.
NASHR:v2p107/r7.anchor: واحتج غيره على أن أصل الراء التفخيم بكونها متمكنة في ظهر اللسان فقربت بذلك من الحنك الأعلى

JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.claim: Iʿtizal means withdrawing or moving away; Jishumi compares the usage in the Cave youths' story and Abraham's withdrawal.
JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.anchor: والاعتزال: التنحي عن الشيء، وكل شيء نحيته فقد عزلته

BURHAN:v4p406/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.claim: The listed ما clauses include relative ما: what is harvested and stored, what was prepared for the seven years, what fathers married, and what people worship besides God.

BURHAN:v1p336/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p336/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p336/r1.claim: Differences by added or omitted letters and words are read only when supported by the Uthmani codices sent to the regions, and are accepted only if they introduce no unasserted ruling.
BURHAN:v1p336/r1.anchor: السابع الاختلاف بالزيادة والنقص فى الحروف والكلم

BURHAN:v1p336/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p336/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p336/r6.claim: Companion readings are stronger than ordinary tafsir as evidence for sound interpretation, and learned specialists use them to establish the proper reading and its meaning.
BURHAN:v1p336/r6.anchor: فهذه الحروف وما شاكلها قد صارت مفسرة للقرآن وقد كان يروى مثل هذا عن بعض التابعين فى التفسير فيستحسن ذلك فكيف إذا روى عن كبار الصحابة ثم صار فى نفس القراءة فهو الآن أكثر من التفسير وأقوى

ITQAN:v2p514#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p514#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p514#2/r6.claim: In وما يعبدون إلا الله, ما is also an exception to the general negative reading before إلا.
ITQAN:v2p514#2/r6.anchor: وإذا اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله

ITQAN:v2p430/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p430/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
ITQAN:v2p430/r1.claim: Abu Malik says إن with kasra in the Qur'an concerns what has not yet happened, while إذ marks what has happened.
ITQAN:v2p430/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال ما كان في القرآن إن بكسر الألف فلم يكن وما كان إذ فقد كان

ITQAN:v2p430/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p430/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p430/r5.claim: Some grammarians classify إذ in 18:16 and 46:11 as causal; most reject this category and read the example in 43:39 as بعد إذ ظلمتم, “after you acted wrongfully.”
ITQAN:v2p430/r5.anchor: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف

DAMGHANI:v1p59/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p59/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p59/r5.claim: Āwā can mean to reach or go to a place, as when they reached the rock or went to the cave.

DAMGHANI:v1p456/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p456/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p456/r1.claim: Nashr can mean spreading or extending mercy, glossed as spreading wind and clouds; rain is grouped with it.
DAMGHANI:v1p456/r1.anchor: النشور البسط قوله تعالى في سورة حم عسق

DAMGHANI:v1p207/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p207/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p207/r4.claim: Mirfaq can mean provision in the youths’ prayer for practical help.
DAMGHANI:v1p207/r4.anchor: المرفق الرزق قوله تعالى في سورة الكهف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r1.claim: The basic sense of نشر is to spread something out fully; its opposite is folding it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r1.anchor: النشر : في الأصل بسط الشيء ومده على ما هو عليه من منتهى جوانبه . ونقيضه : الطي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r2.claim: In figurative usage, نشر الله الموتى means that God brought the dead to life.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r2.anchor: فيقال نشر الله الموتى ، أي ، أحياهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r3.claim: انتشر الناس في حوائجهم means that people dispersed to attend to their affairs.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r4.claim: النشر can also mean a pleasant breeze, and ريح نشر describes a broad, spreading wind.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r4.anchor: والنشر : الريح الطيبة . وريح نشر : منتشرة واسعة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r5.claim: النشوار is the fodder an animal leaves uneaten.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r5.anchor: والنشوار : ما تبقيه الدابة من العلف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r7.claim: In 18:16, نشر means spreading or extending mercy; the same usage is grouped with 42:28.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p583/r7.anchor: والثاني : البسط . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف : ﴿ ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ﴾
